fact: In unincorporated Larimer County, the building final inspection that a Certificate of Occupancy waits on is made after finish grading, and a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy may be issued for 180 days once life-safety issues are corrected, for a $600 fee that is partly refundable.
quote: A final inspection needs to be requested and approved by the Larimer County inspector prior to release of a Certificate of Occupancy. Final Inspection - To be made after finish grading, and the building is completed and ready for occupancy, all plumbing fixtures are set, heating equipment set and working, and final electric is signed off. … A Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) may be issued for 180 days after final inspections are obtained and all life-safety issues have been corrected, in the judgment of the county building inspector. … pay a $600 TCO fee, which is partially refundable if you make all corrections prior to the TCO's expiration.
source_label: Larimer County Building Division, Certificate of Occupancy
notes: Read 2026-09-26 through a fetch tool; plain curl gets a 403, so re-check in a browser. Covers permits the County issues (unincorporated land), not homes inside a town, whose building departments run their own final inspections. The same page lists Planning's landscaping sign-off for commercial buildings only; it names no landscaping requirement for a residential CO.

fact: Wellington's landscape standards apply to new development under site plan review or a subdivision application, and a building permit for an individual single-family house needs no landscape plan.
quote: (b) Applicability. (1) The provisions herein shall apply to all new development or redevelopment subject to site plan review or subdivision application. (2) Building permit applications for individual single-family residences will not require landscape plans. Single-family residences are encouraged to consider the Landscape and Irrigation Design Manual at Section 15-5-40 (c).
source_label: Wellington Municipal Code Sec. 15-5-40(b), Applicability (Municode, Supplement 9 Update 2)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 500257, product 18291) on 2026-09-26.

fact: Wellington's single-family lot standards, including the 75% live-materials front yard and a 50% cap on high-water plants such as irrigated turfgrass on lots under half an acre, apply to lots developed as part of a subdivision; a standalone development that needs no subdivision or site plan application is exempt from both.
quote: (2) Applicability: In addition to landscaping the right-of-way tree lawn, detached and attached single-family parcels developed as part of an overall subdivision, shall meet the following standards. Standalone developments that do not require a subdivision or site plan application are exempt from items (3)a. and b. below. (3) General design standards: a. Landscaping on a single-family lot under one half (½) acre in size shall include no more than fifty percent (50%) of the total landscaped area comprised of high water use plant material such as irrigated turfgrass. b. There shall be a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) live materials between the front of the single-family residential structure and the curb, excluding paved driveway areas.
source_label: Wellington Municipal Code Sec. 15-5-40(i)(2)-(3), Standard Lot Detached and Attached Single-Family Residential Development Landscape Standards (Municode, Supplement 9 Update 2)
notes: Adds the standalone-development exemption that the shared record wellington-code-15-5-40-front-yard-75 leaves out. Whether a custom house on an already-platted lot is 'part of an overall subdivision' or 'standalone' is the Town's call.

fact: On Wellington single-family lots of half an acre or more in the R-1 zone, landscaping may include no more than 25% high-water plant material, such as irrigated turfgrass, and no more than a quarter acre of irrigated ornamental plants.
quote: (j) Large Lot Single-Family Residential Development Landscape Standards. (1) Purpose and intent: To ensure higher water use landscape areas remain close to the perimeter of the residence, therefore preserving the native resources on the outskirts of the property both for purposes of water conservation and preservation of the natural character. (2) Applicability: Landscaping of large single-family rural density lots of one-half (½) acre or more in size (R-1 zone district) shall meet the following standards. (3) General design standards: a. Shall include no more than twenty-five percent (25%) high water use plant material, such as irrigated turfgrass, and no more than one-quarter (¼) acre irrigated, ornamental plant material.
source_label: Wellington Municipal Code Sec. 15-5-40(j), Large Lot Single-Family Residential Development Landscape Standards (Municode, Supplement 9 Update 2)
notes: A cap on live irrigated turfgrass; the subsection does not mention artificial turf. Whether artificial turf counts toward the cap, the remaining landscape or neither is not stated: ask Wellington Planning.

fact: Where Wellington's landscape standards apply, required landscaping must be installed before a certificate of occupancy, and if weather prevents that, the developer posts financial security of 125% of an approved line-item cost estimate until the Town accepts the finished work.
quote: d. Guarantee of installation. Required landscape improvements shall be installed prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy (CO) for all new construction and redeveloped sites. If weather conditions prevent installation, the developer shall post a financial guarantee for the improvements in an amount equal to one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of an approved line-item cost estimate. The guarantee shall be released upon completion of the installation of the landscaping and acceptance by the Town.
source_label: Wellington Municipal Code Sec. 15-5-40(e), Guarantee of installation (Municode, Supplement 9 Update 2)
notes: The section applies to development under site plan review or a subdivision application (Sec. 15-5-40(b)); a single-family building permit needs no landscape plan. How this clause reaches one custom house is not stated: ask Wellington Planning. Copy avoids the word 'guarantee' outside this quote.
